rules.statement: Save files as UTF-8 without a BOM, with LF line endings, and follow the repository's `.editorconfig`.
rules.why: The template sets UTF-8 without BOM and LF as the base file convention for every repository.
rules.check: Look for files added or changed with a BOM, CRLF line endings, or formatting that contradicts `.editorconfig`.

rules.statement: Never commit `PLAN.md`; it is a local, gitignored working file for the plan-then-execute workflow.
rules.why: PLAN.md is the handoff between planner and executor and must never be committed, staged or pushed.
rules.check: Flag any diff that adds or modifies `PLAN.md` in the commit or pull request.

rules.statement: Don't edit project-template-owned files (`.github/instructions/project-template.instructions.md`, `.template/`, `.template-version`, `.githooks/commit-msg`, `docs/decisions/project-template/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/agents/plan-executor.md`, generated commands, prompts, agents and skills, `.copier-answers.yml`); override a rule in `AGENTS.md` or a project instruction file instead.
rules.why: Template updates replace those files and discard any edit made to them.
rules.check: Flag changes to template-owned paths that aren't part of a template update; suggest moving the override into `AGENTS.md` or a project instruction file.

rules.statement: Don't keep an outdated or insecure shape just because existing code already has it: correct it to current practice, and update the comments, docs and decision records it touches in the same change.
rules.why: Existing code, comments and docs show what someone intended when they wrote them. They don't bind later changes, and stale docs mislead.
rules.check: Look for new code that copies a deprecated or insecure pattern from nearby code, or a change in behavior that leaves the comments, docs or ADRs describing it out of date.

rules.statement: Every change that completes planned work adds its entries to the changelog in Keep a Changelog 1.1.0 format: under `## [Unreleased]`, or under the new version's `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` section when releasing, grouped under Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed or Security, with compare links at the end. Leave a changelog in another format in its own style.
rules.why: The template makes writing the changelog the last step of every plan and standardizes on Keep a Changelog.
rules.check: Check that a change consumers can see has a changelog entry under the right section and category heading, and that new release sections come newest first and have compare links.

rules.statement: A change consumers can observe (public API, behavior, validation or security posture, stored data or wire formats) must come with an ADR in `docs/decisions/` recording its decision, added before or in the same pull request.
rules.why: Consumer-observable decisions must be recorded so that nobody re-argues them later. Bug fixes and internal changes don't need one.
rules.check: When a diff changes public API, behavior, validation, security posture, stored data or a wire format, check for a new or existing ADR that covers the decision.

rules.statement: Record a project ADR as a new file numbered from 1000 and replace an outdated one by superseding it, never by rewriting it; numbers below 1000 belong to the template's decisions.
rules.why: Each ADR number names exactly one record, and superseding keeps the history of decisions.
rules.check: Flag edits that change the decision of an existing accepted ADR instead of adding a superseding one, and new project ADRs numbered below 1000.

rules.why: CI runs `.template/Test-AdrIndex.ps1` to check that the index lists every record.
rules.check: A new ADR file has a matching entry in the decisions README.

rules.statement: When a project overrides a template decision, write a project ADR that supersedes the template's ADR and list the override in `AGENTS.md`.
rules.why: Overrides must be explicit so that the template's rule and the project's rule don't silently conflict.
rules.check: A change that departs from a template rule comes with a superseding ADR and an `AGENTS.md` entry.

rules.statement: Never commit secrets, `.env` files, or the contents of the root `secrets/` folder.
rules.why: Secrets must never enter the repository or a prompt.
rules.check: Look for credentials, keys, tokens, `.env` files or files under the root `secrets/` folder in the diff.

rules.statement: Never add a `Co-authored-by:` trailer naming an AI agent, a `Claude-Session:` trailer, or a 'Generated with' line to commits, pull request titles or pull request descriptions.
rules.why: Commits and pull requests record the people who wrote them. A squash merge copies these lines onto the default branch, where only a history rewrite can remove them.
rules.check: Look for agent attribution lines in commit messages and in the pull request title and description.

rules.statement: An `ignore` rule in `.github/dependabot.yml` that holds back an upgrade must have a comment naming the issue that tracks lifting it.
rules.why: A held-back upgrade must stay traceable so that someone lifts it later.
rules.check: Flag new Dependabot `ignore` entries that have no comment pointing to an issue.

rules.statement: When adding or pinning a version of a tool, package or action, use the newest upstream release that is past the dependency cooldown set in the template's decisions.
rules.why: An installed or remembered version says nothing about what is current, and the cooldown guards against brand-new releases.
rules.check: Check that newly pinned versions are current upstream releases past the cooldown, not outdated ones or ones released inside the cooldown window.

rules.statement: Don't leave anything framing finished work as pending: when a change completes an item, remove or update the todo lists, 'remaining' lines in docs and changelog entries that still describe it as open.
rules.why: 'Done' is one fact everywhere. An item counts as done only when no work remains and nothing still frames it as pending.
rules.check: Look for todos, 'remaining' or 'not yet' notes in docs or the changelog that the diff makes obsolete.

rules.statement: Record a lesson learned during a task in an instruction file or an ADR in the same change, never only in an agent's memory.
rules.why: Lessons kept only in an agent's memory are lost to other sessions and tools.
rules.check: When a change corrects a recurring mistake or settles a convention, check that it updates an instruction file or an ADR.
